result.summary: Enables `-Wunused` compiler warning flags in CMake and resolves existing warnings across the codebase. It removes dead functions and methods, comments out or drops unused parameter names, adds `[[maybe_unused]]` attributes, refactors RPC argument parsing using the `Arg<>()` helper, and temporarily patches subtree dependencies.
result.problem: The build system does not enable `-Wunused`, allowing unused code, functions, and parameters to accumulate unnoticed. This can hide bugs where intended functionality was forgotten rather than intentionally dropped (such as #36137).
evidence: PR description: 'We've had a handful of dead code removal PRs over the last month or two... Also well as an instance of what was thought to be dead code, but it'd actually just been forgotten to be used: #36137.'
PR description: 'Enabling some of these flags may also help enforce other stuff, like inline constexpr usage (#35852).'
result.scope_notes: Very wide diff touching 171 files. Contains three `[[nomerge]]` commits modifying subtree code (leveldb, minisketch, libmultiprocess) that require upstream PRs before this can merge. Also contains substantive refactoring in RPC argument parsing (`GetParamIndex` and `Arg<>()`).
result.changed_since_previous: Expanded scope to 171 files and 18 commits, with further cleanup of unused functions and dead code across span, kernel, Qt, and netbase modules.
result.card: Enables `-Wunused` compiler warning flags in CMake to prevent dead code and unused parameters from accumulating across the repository. Without compiler enforcement, unused code accumulates unnoticed and can hide logic errors where variables or parameters were accidentally forgotten (e.g., #36137). The pull request resolves existing warnings across 171 files via dead code removal, parameter omissions, attribute annotations, and RPC argument refactors. Merging is blocked on upstream subtree PRs in Minisketch and libmultiprocess.

risk.why: Wide-ranging mechanical changes and RPC parameter parsing refactors (`GetParamIndex` and `Arg`) could alter command argument handling or introduce subtle behavioral changes across critical subsystems.
